title: Quantum AI-Enhanced IoT-Fog Communication: A Survey from Cybersecurity and Data Privacy Perspective
domain: Quantum AI, IoT-Fog Computing, Cybersecurity, Neurosymbolic AI, Post-Quantum Cryptography, 6G Security
abstract_summary: Comprehensive review of Quantum AI applications for cybersecurity and data privacy in next-generation IoT-Fog architectures. Covers quantum computing principles, QML techniques, Neurosymbolic AI for cyber defence, threat landscapes, industrial and cyber-physical system security, and research challenges for 6G networks.

section_flow.title: Introduction
section_flow.purpose: Establish cybersecurity challenges in 6G/IoT-Fog and motivate Quantum AI solutions

section_flow.title: Quantum AI: Features and Core Concepts
section_flow.purpose: Review quantum computing principles, QML models, and their security applications

section_flow.title: AI Agents and Neurosymbolic AI for Cyber Defence
section_flow.purpose: Explore neural-symbolic integration for explainable threat detection

section_flow.title: Threat Landscape in IoT-Fog Architectures
section_flow.purpose: Analyze security challenges, decentralized threats, and resource constraints

section_flow.title: Security in Industrial and Cyber-Physical Systems
section_flow.purpose: ICS security, QKD/PQC implementation, and distributed IoT-Fog networks

section_flow.title: Discussion, Opportunities, and Open Challenges
section_flow.purpose: Lessons learned, research gaps, and future directions

section_flow.title: Conclusion
section_flow.purpose: Summarize Quantum AI potential for next-generation cybersecurity

writing_recipes.name: Survey Coverage Matrix with Symbolic Indicators
writing_recipes.description: Creating a literature comparison table where each existing survey is evaluated against key topics using symbolic coverage indicators (filled circle for well-covered, half-filled for partially covered, empty for uncovered).
writing_recipes.rhetorical_function: Visually establishes the gap in existing literature and positions the current survey's comprehensive contribution

template.final_row: This Work row with all topics filled

examples: Table I showing 16 existing surveys with 5 coverage dimensions (Quantum AI, IoT, Fog, Privacy, Security)

writing_recipes.name: Concept-to-Application Mapping Table
writing_recipes.description: Presenting foundational concepts (e.g., quantum computing principles) alongside their specific relevance to the application domain (cybersecurity), with author, year, concept, key principle, and relevance columns.
writing_recipes.rhetorical_function: Bridges theoretical concepts to practical applications, making abstract ideas accessible to domain-specific readers

template.structure: One row per foundational concept with explicit application relevance

examples: Table II mapping 13 quantum concepts (Qubits, Entanglement, QNNs, QSVMs, etc.) to cybersecurity relevance

writing_recipes.name: Feature-by-Feature AI Paradigm Comparison Table
writing_recipes.description: Systematically comparing two AI paradigms (e.g., conventional AI Agents vs Neurosymbolic AI Agents) across multiple operational features with detailed descriptions for each paradigm.
writing_recipes.rhetorical_function: Enables readers to understand tradeoffs and select appropriate paradigm for their use case
examples: Table III comparing AI Agents vs Neurosymbolic AI across 12 features (Intrusion Detection, Malware Detection, Zero-Day Response, Explainability, etc.)

writing_recipes.name: Multi-Dimensional Threat Landscape Table
writing_recipes.description: Organizing threat analysis with consistent four-column structure: Aspect, Description, Challenges, Technologies/Strategies, and Opportunities.
writing_recipes.rhetorical_function: Transforms threat analysis into actionable framework by pairing challenges with solution strategies and research opportunities

template.complementary_tables: Multiple tables (IV and V) with consistent structure

examples: Table IV (15 IoT-Fog threat aspects) and Table V (12 threat response aspects) with consistent 4-5 column structure

writing_recipes.name: Lessons Learned Section with Deployment Stratification
writing_recipes.description: Including a dedicated 'Lessons Learned' subsection that synthesizes insights from literature review, organized by deployment tier (Edge/Fog/Cloud) with specific technology mappings.
writing_recipes.rhetorical_function: Provides practitioners with actionable deployment guidance based on architectural constraints

structure: Tier-specific technology recommendations (Edge: lightweight classifiers, Fog: agentic coordination, Cloud: QGANs)
Trade-off analysis (latency vs. accuracy, preprocessing vs. offloading)

examples: Section VI.A Lessons Learned with Edge/Fog/Cloud deployment stratification for QML models

writing_recipes.name: Numbered Challenge Enumeration with Multi-Domain Focus
writing_recipes.description: Organizing future research challenges as numbered subsections (1-7), each covering a distinct domain or technology area (6G, Scalability, PQC, Real-time, Interpretability, Neurosymbolic, Industrial).
writing_recipes.rhetorical_function: Provides comprehensive research agenda with clear domain boundaries for future researchers

template.format: Numbered subsections (1) 6G Wireless Services, (2) Scalability, (3) Post-Quantum Cryptographic Standards, etc.

examples: Section VI.B with 7 numbered challenges: 6G, Scalability, PQC, Real-time Processing, Interpretability, Neurosymbolic AI, Industrial Security

processing_metadata.notes: 800-line survey on Quantum AI for IoT-Fog cybersecurity with strong Neurosymbolic AI coverage. Notable for Survey Coverage Matrix with symbolic indicators and Multi-Dimensional Threat Landscape tables.
